upsert.title: Quasiorganelle therapy for canine histiocytic sarcoma
upsert.center: Michigan State University Veterinary Medical Center
upsert.status: Actively recruiting — current MSU clinical-trials page and August 24, 2026 recruitment announcement
upsert.funding: Funded trial. Trial-associated tests, quasiorganelle treatment, hospitalization, blood/fecal sampling, imaging and treatment of trial-related complications are covered after enrollment; initial evaluation is charged.
upsert.notes: First cohort receives weakened non-disease-causing Listeria-derived quasiorganelle therapy alone; second cohort receives quasiorganelle therapy including gene therapy. Up to 5 visible lesions are allowed with summed longest dimensions under 15 cm. Weekly treatment x4, then 2 weeks off, repeated for a total 16-week treatment period. While enrolled, dogs should not live with someone pregnant or planning pregnancy.

upsert.title: CARE trial: autophagy inhibition plus radiation for canine glioma
upsert.center: UC Davis Weill School of Veterinary Medicine / Translational Brain Tumor Center
upsert.status: Actively recruiting — UC Davis recruitment announcement published September 3, 2026
upsert.contacts: UC Davis Veterinary Center for Clinical Trials — (530) 754-1954; contact Dr. Christine Toedebusch / study team via the official UC Davis page
upsert.funding: Study covers all study procedures and provides $4,000 toward radiation therapy; owners remain responsible for radiation costs beyond the study contribution.
upsert.notes: Combined Autophagy inhibition and Radiation to improve Efficacy in canine glioma (CARE). Dogs receive an experimental IV autophagy-inhibiting drug twice weekly for four weeks concurrently with standard radiation therapy, with brain-tumor biopsy before and after treatment. Current UC Davis materials state dogs with MRI-suspected glioma may be screened; final eligibility is determined by the neuro-oncology team.

upsert.title: PRISM: radiation-treatment access and funded follow-up for canine glioma
upsert.center: UC Davis Weill School of Veterinary Medicine / Translational Brain Tumor Center
upsert.status: Actively recruiting — UC Davis recruitment announcement published September 3, 2026
upsert.contacts: UC Davis Veterinary Center for Clinical Trials — (530) 754-1954; contact Dr. Christine Toedebusch / PRISM study team via the official UC Davis page
upsert.funding: Radiation pathway provides $3,000 toward radiation treatment and covers trial-related follow-up care, including follow-up visits and brain MRI examinations. The observational/palliative pathway instead provides $3,000 toward the initial diagnostic workup and covers trial-related follow-up care.
upsert.notes: OTHER TREATMENT-ACCESS OPPORTUNITY — not an experimental anticancer-treatment trial. PRISM is primarily a research/monitoring study. Dogs in its radiation pathway may receive standard radiation therapy according to the owner's wishes, with $3,000 study support toward radiation and funded trial-related follow-up. The study also has a non-treatment observational/palliative pathway. Keep separate from the strict experimental-treatment matcher.
